categories.main_business_segments: Prologis operates two primary business segments: (1) Real Estate, which includes rental operations and development of logistics facilities, and (2) Strategic Capital, which manages co-investment ventures with institutional partners. The Real Estate segment generates the majority of revenue through leasing, property management, development, acquisitions, and dispositions, while the Strategic Capital segment earns fees and promotes from managing assets for third-party investors.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Prologis leverages advanced property management systems, sustainable building technologies, and data analytics to optimize logistics facilities. The company emphasizes sustainable development, including LED lighting, solar generation, energy storage, and efficient building design, and integrates digital tools and analytics for portfolio management and customer solutions. Development expertise, procurement capabilities, and the Prologis Essentials platform underpin its operational methods.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Prologis serves over 6,500 customers globally, primarily logistics users such as e-commerce, retail, transportation, third-party logistics, and manufacturing companies. Major customers include Amazon, Home Depot, FedEx, UPS, DHL, Walmart, and other large-scale distributors and logistics providers. Its facilities are critical for supply chain operations, including last-mile delivery, import/export, and regional distribution.
categories.geographic_coverage: Prologis operates in 20 countries across North America, Europe, Asia, and Latin America, with a portfolio of approximately 1.3 billion square feet. The largest concentrations are in the U.S. (notably California, New Jersey/New York, Chicago, Dallas/Ft. Worth, and other major logistics hubs), with significant holdings in Europe (UK, Germany, France, Netherlands), Asia (Japan, China), and Latin America (Mexico, Brazil, Canada).
categories.supply_chain_position: Prologis is positioned as a downstream provider in the supply chain, owning, developing, and managing logistics real estate that serves as critical infrastructure for warehousing, distribution, and last-mile delivery. Its facilities are used by customers for storage, fulfillment, and distribution of goods to end consumers and businesses.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Prologis focuses on expanding its high-quality, well-located logistics portfolio, driving organic growth through rent increases and development, and growing its Strategic Capital business. Innovation priorities include sustainability (renewable energy, green building certifications), digital transformation, supply chain analytics, and customer-centric solutions via Prologis Essentials. The company also invests in emerging logistics technologies through Prologis Ventures.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through rental income from operating leases, including recoveries of property expenses, and through development and management fees. Strategic Capital revenues come from asset and property management fees, transactional fees, and performance-based promotes from co-investment ventures. Prologis also realizes gains from property dispositions and contributions to ventures.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Prologis is the global leader in logistics real estate, with a scale and geographic reach unmatched by most competitors. It faces competition from regional, national, and global logistics property owners, developers, and investment managers, including Blackstone, GLP, Goodman, and other REITs and private equity firms. Its competitive advantages include portfolio scale, prime locations, customer relationships, and integrated service offerings.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2024, Prologis had total assets of $95.3 billion, consolidated revenues of $8.2 billion, and net earnings attributable to common stockholders of $3.7 billion. The company maintains high occupancy (95.8%), strong liquidity ($7.4 billion), and a robust balance sheet with investment-grade credit ratings. Prologis has demonstrated consistent growth in rents, NOI, and assets under management, with ongoing development and acquisition activity supporting future expansion.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Prologis differentiates itself through its global scale, strategic locations in high-barrier, high-growth markets, and integrated platform of logistics solutions. The company emphasizes sustainability, operational efficiency, and customer-centric services (Prologis Essentials), offering unique value in supply chain resiliency, fulfillment speed, and ESG leadership. Its ability to provide comprehensive solutions, deep market expertise, and innovative technologies sets it apart from competitors.
